title: Aurora Cloud x Redwood Intro & Discovery
summary: Intro/partner discovery between Redwood (AE+SE) and Aurora Cloud (partnerships + infra). Discussed Aurora's GPU fleet (A100/H100/next-gen), integration models (marketplace, managed infra, co-sell), technical compatibility with Redwood private/Dedicated, networking (VPC peering, private link), security (KMS/HSM, SOC2), and an initial ask for benchmark tests and a technical deep dive. Agreed next steps: run perf tests, share security pack, schedule deep-dive next week.
topics: benchmarking Redwood runtime on Aurora H100 nodes
next_steps: Priya to run a quick Redwood inference latency/cost benchmark on Aurora H100 80GB nodes and share results (due 2026-11-29)
Liam to send partner one-pager, pricing bands, and security pack (SOC2 + SOC2 Type II summary) by EOD 2026-11-23
Schedule technical deep-dive with Aurora infra team week of 2026-11-30 (Jordan to propose times)
action_items: Priya Kapoor: run latency + throughput benchmark on Aurora H100(80GB) and Lambda-quantized configs; due 2026-11-29
Liam Chen: send partner one-pager, pricing bands, and security docs (SOC2, ISO summary); due 2026-11-23
Jin Soo Kim (Aurora): provide H100 node spec sheet and networking diagram (VPC substacks, private link); due 2026-11-25
transcript:
Meeting header
15:00 UTC 
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Mills (Redwood Solutions); Marta Alvarez (Aurora Partnerships), Ethan Park (BD), Jin Soo Kim (Infra), Rajiv Menon (GPU Sales)

Summary: quick intro, run through Aurora's fleet and GTM, technical compat questions, and next steps for benchmarks and deep-dive.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Liam): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're excited to chat through Aurora's GPU offering and how Redwood could play with your infra, hope that's the plan today
00:22 Speaker 2 (Marta): yes great to meet you all, thanks for taking the time, we got Rajiv and Jin Soo on to talk tech and go-to-market, and Ethan for the partnership side
00:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): quick from our side, i'm Priya se on infra and performance, i'll mainly focus on technical compat and the benchmark ask, liam will cover partner motion and commercials
00:50 Speaker 1 (Liam): yeah, and just to level set, Redwood runs hosted api, dedicated reserved pools and private deploys for customers, our core is predictable latency and cost controls, we often work with cloud partners to certify instance types and co-sell
01:12 Speaker 4 (Rajiv): fantastic, so aurora's angle is we have a growing fleet of H100 blades, plus an A100 hot lane, and we're launching next-gen 9k-series later q1, we want to position as a preferred infra for inference partners, curious what you need to validate
01:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): biggest things are kernel compatibility, memory footprint for kv cache, and the perf for long-running chat workloads, e.g., 8k-32k context, how you handle kv cache offload and streaming, and also quantization profiles (4-bit/8-bit)
02:02 Speaker 5 (Jin Soo): right, we support NCCL, of course, and have optimized drivers, and some customers use NVLink for multi-gpu sharding, we also offer isolated racks for private customers with dedicated top-of-rack switches
02:25 Speaker 1 (Liam): how do you expose networking? we usually need private connectivity — VPC peering or private-link style — because some of our private customers require no egress to public internet
02:40 Speaker 5 (Jin Soo): we do VPC peering, and we can do private link, we also support on-prem rack lift-and-shift but that's more bespoke, there may be slight naming differences in our docs, will share the exact network diagram
03:00 Speaker 3 (Priya): perfect, and on security, do you have KMS integration or HSM options? our customers want BYOK and audit logs
03:10 Speaker 4 (Rajiv): yes, we have HSM integrations with Gemalto and AWS CloudHSM for VPC customers, and we can surface audit logs to a SIEM, SOC2 in flight but we already have ISO27001 and some customers run their own key management
03:30 Speaker 2 (Marta): commercially, we anticipate a partner band model — revenue share or margin add on infra fees, curious what redwood typically expects for co-sell margins
03:45 Speaker 1 (Liam): we generally aim for a model where infra partners can attach a consumption margin and we have a revenue share for referrals; we'll share typical bands but it varies by commitment/scale, liam // liam: also depends on dedicated vs hosted
04:05 Speaker 6 (Ethan): on go-to-market, we can support marketplace listing and joint webinars; we have a channel program and prefer co-marketing commitments for preferred partners
04:25 Speaker 3 (Priya): back to technical: one pain is model lifecycle — can your infra support multiple pinned model versions and fast rollbacks? i.e., can we pin a model variant per tenant and have the orchestration layer respect that without heavy re-warm?
04:50 Speaker 5 (Jin Soo): yes, we can reserve capacity per tenant on dedicated racks, and use pre-warm images, but the warm-up time depends on model size, network storage latency for weights, and whether kv cache persisted across restarts
05:15 Speaker 1 (Liam): that's key, because our serving runtime relies on a warmed kv cache for long-chat flows to hit latency sLOs, sometimes we recommend caching at the infra layer to avoid cold starts
05:35 Speaker 3 (Priya): and about quantization, do you provide BF16 or TF32 support out of the box? some of our kernels prefer BF16; we've seen slight numeric diffs and we need to track quality regressions in evals
05:55 Speaker 5 (Jin Soo): we support BF16 and TF32, and we have a quantization lab for customers that want custom 4-bit pipelines, though note some ops may change latency characteristics
06:20 Speaker 1 (Liam): could you speak to the typical slot sizes you sell? e.g., single H100-80GB vs multi-gpu pinned instances, because our batching and throughput pricing models rely on per-slot throughput estimations
06:35 Speaker 4 (Rajiv): we offer single-card 80GB H100 instances, 2x and 4x NVLink binned nodes and also some rack-level isolated pools, pricing varies by commitment, we'll share a spec/pricing spreadsheet after
06:55 Speaker 3 (Priya): great, the other ask is we'd like to run an initial benchmark: run 75/25 mix of chat gen and embeddings, measure p50/p95 latency, throughput, token cost, and memory usage for LlamaX-70B (our internal test), and a smaller 13B for scale tests
07:20 Speaker 5 (Jin Soo): we can provision test nodes, you can run your workload, or we can run a managed benchmark with redwood engineers if you prefer, we have automation for perf harnesses
07:40 Speaker 1 (Liam): ideal is we do the run together — priya runs the client harness from redwood side, jin soo owns the infra configs, that way we rule out config drift and get a clean chart
07:55 Speaker 2 (Marta): timeline wise, we want to show momentum to our sales teams; if benchmarks go well, we want to list redwood as preferred infra in q1 collateral
08:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): also, small note, sometimes we see transcriptions where people say K-V cash instead of KV cache, and the docs get weird, but it's fine
08:25 Speaker 6 (Ethan): haha, yeah i've seen that. on compliance, can redwood share SOC2 summary and any penetration test results? we need to show partners the compliance posture
08:40 Speaker 1 (Liam): yes we'll attach SOC2 type II report summary and a security pack; but full reports are gated under NDA, we'll start with summaries and a risk matrix
08:55 Speaker 5 (Jin Soo): any special needs for egress controls? some customers require no public egress from model endpoints, only to a private s3 within their vpc
09:10 Speaker 3 (Priya): we support egress locking and private s3 endpoints for private deploys, that is a requirement for several regulated customers, we do also offer canary and A-B rollouts for model changes
09:30 Speaker 4 (Rajiv): also curious about your dedicated offering — do you run the control plane in our region or is it managed by you? locality matters for some customers
09:45 Speaker 1 (Liam): for Dedicated we can run a private control plane in your VPC region, or we can do a managed control plane with private connectivity; for private/on-prem we provide a packaged control plane that you can host behind your subnet and we ship the infra manager as an operator
10:10 Speaker 5 (Jin Soo): good. technical nit: what's your approach to KV cache persistence across restarts, do you use local NVMe or remote s3 backed snapshots?
10:25 Speaker 3 (Priya): we use a hybrid: in-memory + optional prefix/KV caching to a local SSD for fast warm-up and snapshot to object store for longer-term persistence; the runtime orchestrator manages cache expiry and pre-warms for pinned models
10:50 Speaker 6 (Ethan): question on pricing — if a customer is on aurora committed capacity, do you expect to charge marketplace rates or partner-discounted rates?
11:05 Speaker 1 (Liam): we negotiate partner tiers — if infra partner provides committed capacity with a discount, we pass on part of savings to the end-customer and share the rest; exact bands we'll put in the partner doc
11:20 Speaker 2 (Marta): ok so next steps — run benchmarks, share docs, schedule technical deep-dive — anything else?
11:30 Speaker 3 (Priya): one more: can aurora provide a test account with monitoring hooks (prometheus/grafana metrics) so we can correlate token latency to infra metrics during benchmarks
11:45 Speaker 5 (Jin Soo): yes, we'll provision a sandbox account with grafana dashboards and prometheus exporters for the test cluster, we'll share creds via the secure channel
12:00 Speaker 1 (Liam): brilliant. we'll also share a small eval prompt set so we can measure quality regressions post-quantization; we don't want perf at the cost of quality, so we'll track that in the benchmark spreadsheet
12:20 Speaker 2 (Marta): perfect, that sounds like a plan, let's sync up timeline and names for action items
12:35 Speaker 1 (Liam): recap: Priya to run benchmark and share results, Liam to send partner one-pager and security pack, Jin Soo to provide infra spec and test account, Jordan to schedule deep-dive next week. we'll aim to have results by 2026-11-29
12:55 Speaker 3 (Priya): thanks all, excited to see the H100 perf numbers, and if all looks good we can move to a pilot for a joint customer in q1
13:10 Speaker 6 (Ethan): great, thanks everyone, we'll follow up on partnership ops and marketing ASAP
13:22 Speaker 1 (Liam): thanks folks, talk soon, bye

End of call
